To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reaction of superoxide anion radical with α-tocopherols in acetonitricle solution leads to the formation of an unstable primary oxidation product that is further oxidized by O2, yielding a secondary, more persistent product that can be further oxidized to α-T dimer and quinone.
the reaction of tocopherols with superoxide anions (O2−), generated by the electroreduction of molecular oxygen (O2), is different in dry acetontrile and in aqueously buffered acetonitrile.
the reaction of O2− with α-T in dry acetonitriile leads to the formation of two compounds (designated A, and B) in equimolar amount.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reactions of α-T with reactive oxygen species.
the oxidation mechanism of α-T in aprotic conditions.
elucidating the mechanism of the reactions of O2− with α-T in aprotic (acetonitrile) and protic (aqueous acetonitrilie) conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
α-tocopheroxyl radical, the product of α-tocophenol oxidation by O2−, can be reduced by the same radical, and the reaction can be considered to be a redox reaction.
α-tocopherols are very susceptible to oxidation, and that the oxidation products depend upon the medium and the reaction conditions.
α-T is oxidized by O2− to an unstable primary intermediate, and this intermediate is further oxidized to the secondary stable intermediate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
α-tocopherols are oxidized to α-T dimer, α-T dihydroxy dimenthyl ether, α-T dimenthyl hydroperoxide, and α-T quinone by O2− in aprotic conditions.
the oxidation of α-T to its quinone by O2− in protic conditions proceeds by a one-electron mechanism, while the same reaction under aprotic condition proceeds by a two-electron mechanism.

α-T is oxidized in aprotic media by O2−, forming a primary, unstable intermediate that is further oxidized to the secondary intermediate, and that the secondary intermediate is oxidized to the final products.
The main takeaway from our work is that
O2− is not the only reactive species involved in the oxidation of α-T in protic conditions, but it is the main reactive species involved in α-T oxidation in aprotic conditions.
α-T can be oxidized by O2−, which may play an important role in the oxidation process of α-T.
O2− reacts with α-tocopherols in aprotic media to produce a stable oxidation product that can be reduced by ascorbic acid or LiAlH4 back to α-tocopheral.
